final.summary: The ETP stop from early afternoon to late afternoon held wastewater in the equalization tank, which then rose and fell as stored water was treated after restart. Outfall pH stayed near neutral through the whole treatment interval, and power after the gap followed the expected load with no replay. Together this shows the batch water went through working treatment before discharge.

explanations.label: Normal operation: batch wastewater treated through working ETP
Bypass: untreated wastewater sent around ETP to outfall
Aeration cut: ETP inflow passed but blowers/power cut
ETP stopped then equalization tank overflowed untreated
Meter fault: one or more feeds unreliable for the stretch

key_evidence.why: Tank rose from 0.43 to 0.81 and stayed below full, showing inflow was held during the claimed stop.
Tank balance within tolerance with unaccounted -7.5 m3, showing arriving water was stored, not lost by another route.
Outfall pH stayed near neutral with max 7.74, showing no raw alkaline water reached the outfall.
Power averaged 60.7 kW against 64.3 kW expected with only 0.022 share below band, showing aeration followed load.
Power showed no identical stretch to the prior day, ruling out a replayed feed hiding a cut.

final.scope_line: Based on flow, power, pH, conductivity and tank level records for 2026-10-13 14:00 to 2026-10-14 18:00. Does not measure every pollutant.
limitations: ETP power S3 has no readings from 2026-10-13 14:00 to 2026-10-13 23:05, so aeration during the stop and early restart cannot be checked from power; assessment there rests on tank storage, flow restart and pH.

ETP inflow S2 and outfall flow S4a were flat at 0.0 from 2026-10-13 14:00 to 2026-10-13 17:00, which is expected for a stopped ETP but means those feeds are set aside as unreliable for that flat stretch; other separate signals still establish the claim.
No lab BOD results were available in the case period, so organic pollutant removal is not directly measured.
Factory logbook and maintenance record are claims only and were tested against signals, not taken as fact.

result.note: ETP balance: treated flow reaching the outfall vs outfall flow (same time). Boundary balance: intake vs outfall + losses + sludge water + tank storage change (reuse cancels). Tank balance: wastewater arriving (estimated from intake) vs ETP inflow + storage change; unaccounted water left the tank another way, or was intake water that never became wastewater. null means a required signal is under 80% coverage.
